conventions.convention: The moment-only mixed model has fixed X, Z, and β; centered square-integrable b and ε are independent random elements. G and R may be singular, and Gaussianity is an additional assumption.
The Gaussian branch assumes AC and joint multivariate normality of the concatenated vector (b, ε), with covariance diag(G, R); singular component covariances remain admissible.
Error contrasts use an n by (n−p) column-basis matrix K spanning col(X)⊥, with full-column-rank X and p<n; the contrast vector is KᵀY.
Known-covariance GLS uses the same fixed positive-definite covariance V under every Pβ. Its exact guarantees do not extend automatically to estimated V.
REML fixes X and a contrast basis K independently of θ, requires Vθ positive definite, and compares covariance parameters only within that fixed design.

Missingness is specified by a measurable finite-pattern kernel separately from the response law. MCAR means no dependence on the full responses, permitting dependence on declared covariates; MAR is pattern-specific dependence only through that pattern's observed responses and covariates.
BLUP optimality compares affine predictors with fixed coefficients that are unbiased for E[b]=0 for every fixed β; prediction-error covariance is minimized in positive-semidefinite order.
Variance-component identifiability concerns the target ψ(β,θ)=θ in the full family with β ranging over Rᵖ; it does not require identifiability of β or full rank of X.

load_bearing.statement: A finite-dimensional linear mixed model has Y=Xβ+Zb+ε, fixed X, Z, β, centered square-integrable b and ε, Cov(b)=G, Cov(ε)=R, and independence of b and ε. G and R are symmetric positive semidefinite.

For the moment model Y=Xβ+Zb+ε of def-linear-mixed-model, the marginal covariance is Cov(Y)=V:=ZGZᵀ+R. This identity uses only the stated means, covariances, and independence; it does not require Gaussianity.
The Gaussian branch of def-linear-mixed-model adds the assumption that, under AC, the concatenated vector (b, ε) has law N_{q+n}(0,diag(G,R)).
For full-column-rank X∈R^{n×p} with p<n, an error-contrast matrix K∈R^{n×(n−p)} has columns forming a basis of col(X)⊥. Thus K has full column rank and XᵀK=0.
Assume AC. Let (U₁,U₂) be jointly multivariate normal with mean (m₁,m₂) and covariance diag(S,T), where S and T may be singular positive-semidefinite matrices. Then U₁ and U₂ are independent.

For a linear mixed model with full-column-rank fixed X and known V=Cov(Y) positive definite, β̂_GLS=(XᵀV⁻¹X)⁻¹XᵀV⁻¹Y is unbiased, has covariance (XᵀV⁻¹X)⁻¹, and has no larger variance in any contrast than any other linear unbiased estimator. Gaussianity is not assumed.
Assume AC and the Gaussian mixed model. For full-column-rank X with p<n and an error-contrast matrix K, KᵀY has law N_{n−p}(0,KᵀVK), independent of β. KᵀVK may be singular.
Assume AC. For d≥1 and symmetric positive-definite Σ, N_d(m,Σ) has Lebesgue density (2π)^(−d/2)det(Σ)^(−1/2)exp(−(x−m)ᵀΣ⁻¹(x−m)/2).

Assume AC, nonempty Θ, and a declared Gaussian covariance-component parameterization with Vθ=ZGθZᵀ+Rθ positive semidefinite. In P_{β,θ}=N_n(Xβ,Vθ), the target ψ(β,θ)=θ is identifiable if and only if θ↦Vθ is injective on Θ.

concerns.concern: Facts & Assumptions F2 states that 'correlation is covariance divided by the product of the positive standard deviations' and cites def-moments-variance-and-covariance. The opened supplier defines absolute moments, mean, variance, and covariance, but contains no definition of correlation. Verification 2.1 uses this additional convention. The ICC calculation and its zero-variance caveats are sound; the citation attributes a definition absent from its supplier.

seams_checked.note: The actual contract requires explicit scientific roles and a separately specified observation mechanism without implying independence, missingness, or adequacy. The mixed-model and missingness definitions preserve these requirements; the dropout counterexample specifies its kernel separately.

The supplier fixes X and supplies EβY=Xβ without covariance or Gaussian assumptions. Batch 7 adds rank and covariance hypotheses explicitly. GLS whitening produces a full-rank design and covariance I, satisfying the actual Gauss–Markov theorem with σ²=1; competing linear estimators remain linear after whitening.

The replication definition's fixed-treatment model is a random-intercept specialization of the moment-only LMM. It explicitly adds mutual independence, common variances, and balanced measurements. Its assignment-averaged branch separately retains treatment variance and cross-covariances.

The nested batch definition uses the finite-moment random-intercept form with fixed process offsets and explicitly adds mutual independence and common variances. Its covariance and mean-variance theorem requires no Gaussianity and handles singleton batches and zero component variances.
